content.user_title: Map Skills to Clear Proficiency Levels
content.value_statement: Learning plans often use vague levels and omit prerequisites. This skill maps skills to recognized frameworks, measurable indicators, and coherent assessments.
actual_capabilities: Maps skill outcomes to CEFR, Bloom's Taxonomy, and DigComp frameworks.
Defines measurable indicators for A1 through C2 proficiency levels.
Checks learning sequences for regression and missing prerequisites.
Matches assessment formats and rubrics to the intended proficiency level.
Applies five coherence checks for naming, progression, prerequisites, and connectivity.
limitations: Does not verify framework claims against external sources in real time.
Requires curriculum context, learner goals, and prerequisites for reliable mapping.
Provides guidance rather than accredited assessment or certification decisions.
Cannot measure a learner's actual performance without submitted evidence.

use_cases.title: Build a course progression
use_cases.description: Create a non-regressive sequence of lessons with clear prerequisites and proficiency targets.

use_cases.title: Align workplace training
use_cases.description: Define observable competency levels and suitable assessments for a team training program.

use_cases.title: Improve self-study plans
use_cases.description: Turn broad learning goals into staged skills, practice tasks, and evidence of progress.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: classify one skill
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a starting proficiency level.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the skill “write a basic API specification” to a CEFR level. Give three measurable indicators and one suitable assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: design a progression
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A1 to B1 progression for SQL query skills. List prerequisites, measurable indicators, and practice activities for each level.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: audit a curriculum
prompt_templates.scenario: You have an existing lesson sequence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this curriculum for proficiency regression, missing prerequisites, duplicate skill names, and isolated skills. Recommend specific corrections.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: align assessments
prompt_templates.prompt: Align these learning objectives, activities, and rubric criteria to CEFR and Bloom levels. Identify mismatches and propose revised evidence requirements.

output_examples.input: Map “debug a simple program” to A2 proficiency.
output: Indicators: identifies a visible error, follows a provided debugging process, and verifies a basic fix.
Assessment: correct one guided program defect and explain the change.

output_examples.input: Check a sequence that teaches B1 data modeling before A2 database concepts.
output: Reason: B1 data modeling depends on foundational database concepts.
Recommendation: add A2 concepts before the B1 modeling lesson.

best_practices: Provide learner context, available time, and prior knowledge before requesting a mapping.
Use observable actions and evidence instead of subjective labels such as easy or difficult.
Review every progression for prerequisites and non-decreasing proficiency levels.
anti_patterns: Do not assign levels only because a topic feels advanced.
Do not use one assessment format for every proficiency level.
Do not introduce dependent skills before their foundations are taught.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses CEFR, Bloom's Taxonomy, DigComp, cognitive load guidance, and prerequisite checks.

faq.question: Can it map technical skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for specification, coding, and other professional skills.

faq.question: Does it certify learner proficiency?
faq.answer: No. It helps design indicators and assessments, but it does not issue certification.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the skill, learner background, desired outcome, time available, and existing prerequisites.

faq.question: Can it review an existing curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify regressions, missing prerequisites, inconsistent naming, and isolated skills.

faq.question: Is CEFR limited to language learning?
faq.answer: The skill applies CEFR-style progression descriptors to broader skills as a planning framework.
